title: Pirc Defense: the ideas
line: Black lets White build a center, puts a bishop on the long diagonal, and strikes at the center later.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its king two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn in front of your queen one square. It keeps White's pawn out of e5 for now.

also.e7e5: That is the open game, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.
also.c7c5: That is the Sicilian Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.
also.e7e6: That is the French Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.
also.c7c6: That is the Caro-Kann Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.
also.d7d5: That is the Scandinavian Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.
also.g7g6: That is the Modern Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.
also.g8f6: That is the Alekhine Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to hit the pawn on e4.

also.e7e5: That is also played. This lesson brings the knight out.
also.g7g6: That leads to the Modern Defense, a close cousin. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.after: Black lets White keep two pawns in the center: White gets space now, and Black plans to attack them later.

steps.text: Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.

also.e7e5: That also works. This lesson goes on with the Pirc.

steps.after: White develops calmly. This is the Classical Variation.

steps.text: Put the bishop on g7. Behind your knight, it aims down the long diagonal at the pawn on d4.
Castle. Your king goes to safety, and a rook comes toward the center.
Bring the bishop out to hit the knight that guards d4.

also.e7e5: That strikes at once, and it is also played. This lesson pins the knight first.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It hits the pawn on d4 too.
Now strike at the center: push the pawn on e7 two squares.
steps.after: Your pawn hits the pawn on d4, and White can take it, push past it or keep the tension.

summary: The Pirc lets White build a center, aims a bishop at it from the side, and strikes at it once the pieces are out.
